tasks.spec:
You are a code worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge (Python 3.12). Edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit, push, or touch .git. You own exactly: bench/affordance_map.py, tests/test_affordance_map.py, bench/affordance_known_gaps.json. Edit nothing else; story packages under data/ and tests/fixtures/ are ground truth and stay unchanged.

CONTEXT: bench/affordance_map.py (read it and tests/test_affordance_map.py first) builds, per scene transition gate, the "affordances" a player must act on, for .plans/scene-affordance-e2e.md. Reading its output for data/stories/continuity-initiative scene 1A shows it is noisy. A later tool (the hosted E2E test) will check that the narration names each affordance, so a wrong affordance is a false alarm. Fix exactly these defects, story-agnostically (no hard-coded ids or words):

1. An affordance must be a thing, place or person the player's ACTION must name. Derive affordances from (a) the object groups of a knowledge item's action_evidence (all groups after the first, resolved to entities by name/alias, whole word, case-insensitive), (b) the affordances of the sources that produce facts in its `requires` chain. Do NOT add a knowledge item's `entity_ids` as affordances when the item has action_evidence: entity_ids mix participants and learned outcomes (for example k_sl_1a_b_r1 lists park_bench, a place the player only learns about from the memory card). Only when a player-earned item has NO action_evidence, fall back to entity_ids, minus the protagonist. Never emit the protagonist (package.protagonist_id) as an affordance.
2. A thing that a source itself reveals (a hidden item the source's own established facts or world reveal effects produce, for example the memory card taped under the drawer) is an OUTCOME of that source, not an affordance of it. Record such entities in a separate per-source list "reveals" (entity ids) and keep them out of "affordances". They remain valid as visible-after affordances of LATER sources that require this one (with revealed_by set).
3. Add to every affordance its "aliases" (the entity's alias tuple) so a reader can match narration without reloading the world. Add to each scene entry "location": {"id", "name", "aliases"} for SceneMetadata.location_id, and "protagonist_id" at the top level.
4. Keep all four checks working on the corrected affordances. Update bench/affordance_known_gaps.json by regenerating it with the CLI after the fix; the list will shrink. Update tests: add a regression test per defect above (protagonist excluded; entity_ids ignored when action_evidence exists; a source's own reveal is in "reveals" not "affordances"; aliases and location present), and keep the existing tests passing or updated with a reason in notes.md. The 1A map must still list michelle_drawer, michelle_workstation, and kristin_laptop as affordances (as visible_at_entry) and memory_card must be in a "reveals" list.

HOW TO RUN: TMPDIR=/tmp uv run pytest -q -n0 tests/test_affordance_map.py ; TMPDIR=/tmp uv run python -m bench.affordance_map --package data/stories/continuity-initiative --out /tmp/cm.json ; TMPDIR=/tmp uv run ruff check --fix bench/affordance_map.py tests/test_affordance_map.py && TMPDIR=/tmp uv run ruff format bench/affordance_map.py tests/test_affordance_map.py. No network or model calls. Also write ./notes.md at the worktree root (the check excludes it from the diff; do not git add it) listing what changed, the new finding counts per check on both packages, and assumptions.
tasks.verified: owned files only; tests, ruff and CLI pass; 1A map has drawer, workstation, laptop as affordances and memory_card as a reveal
